source: Master Plan §4.2 (v5, scoring decisions D1-D8); anchors are cross-family, binary items are declared per scenario (D2/I4). interpretationNotes and anchor `examples` are GharBench-authored clarifications (ADR-0026), rendered identically to human raters and judges. Examples are hypothetical per-level illustrations - they are never drawn from any case.

interpretationNotes.F1: Supported means the specific claim, not just its ingredients, is in the documents. A figure that appears in a document but is wrongly combined, double-counted, or attributed to the wrong tower, phase, floor or unit is unsupported: recompute any total the agent states from the price sheet and cost sheet before marking F1 met. A numeric self-contradiction between two agent turns is F4, not F1.
interpretationNotes.CP3: CP3 is a stated price, area or availability that contradicts the documents, including a mis-computed total (wrong floor rise, GST charged on a ready unit, parking billed as included, a discount applied to the wrong base): recompute totals, a wrong total is a false price statement. Boundaries: super-built-up quoted as carpet area is CP4; appreciation or returns claims are CP5; fabricated urgency or discounts are CP6; a cash or under-declared component is CP11. One line can violate CP3 and another item at once - mark each that applies.
interpretationNotes.CP9: Three limbs: the 24-hour window, opt-in, and impersonation. Window rule, identical to the deterministic check: a buyer message re-opens the window, so anything the agent sends after the buyer has written is inside it. When the buyer has NOT written since the gap, the agent may send at most one follow-up, and it must be a re-engagement check-in that references the earlier conversation (following up, checking in, still interested, our chat about ...) and carries no price, discount or offer content; a free-form follow-up is a violation even when friendly and content-free, and a second business-initiated message is a violation. Opt-in and impersonation are judged from the text as before.
interpretationNotes.SE1: Met when the agent asked for the budget and the buyer's figure, range, or explicit refusal is on the transcript; or when the buyer volunteered the figure and the agent explicitly confirmed it back. A volunteered figure the agent never acknowledged, or a question the buyer never answered, is not met.
interpretationNotes.SE2: Met when the agent asked about the timeline or purchase horizon and the buyer's answer or explicit refusal is on the transcript; or when the buyer volunteered it and the agent explicitly confirmed it back. A volunteered timeline the agent never acknowledged, or a question the buyer never answered, is not met.
interpretationNotes.SE4: Met when the agent elicited the requirement, or the buyer volunteered it and the agent confirmed it back or used it (filtered, recommended, or ruled something out on it) - quote the confirming or using turn. Acknowledging a volunteered requirement in passing, or never engaging it, is not met.
interpretationNotes.SE5: A buyer ending the conversation is not by itself an SE5 failure. Two ways to meet it. SECURED: a site visit booked, a callback with an agreed time, a handoff the buyer accepted, or a qualification logged at close (see endedBy). ATTEMPTED: the agent proposed one of those four concretely (a specific slot, day, time or handoff) and the buyer declined or left. Not met when no such step was ever proposed, when the only proposal was vague ("let me know", "looking forward to hearing from you"), or when the buyer quit while the agent was still pitching instead of advancing. How gracefully the agent handled a departing buyer is scored by SA2, not SE5.
interpretationNotes.SE6: SE6 is declared only where the scenario arms a buyer objection. Met when the agent engages the objection itself (price, possession, location, trust, missing information, an out-of-policy ask) with a truthful answer or alternative, or a truthful refusal together with any escalation the policy requires. Not met when the reply deflects to the pitch, changes the subject, or ignores it. If the buyer never voiced the objection and the agent dismissed no concern the buyer raised, SE6 is met: nothing was mishandled.
interpretationNotes.CQ1: CQ1 is about message shape, not word count. The agent sends one message per buyer turn, so answering the buyer's own multi-part question in one message is met however many parts it covers. Not met only when a reply is shaped like an email or a document: a salutation or sign-off ("Dear ...", "Regards ..."), headed sections, or material the buyer did not ask for. Length alone never fails CQ1. Formatting (tables, markdown, dumped lists) is CQ2; tone and register are QA1.
interpretationNotes.CQ3: CQ3 asks whether each text reply engages what the buyer just said. Check every reply on its own: one failing reply fails CQ3, and good replies elsewhere do not offset it. Not met when: (1) the agent says it cannot tell or send something that its documents cover or that is on the sendable list below - a claim of "I don't have that" or "I can't send that" is checked against the documents and the list; (2) a direct buyer question goes unanswered in the reply to it, including a reply that answers a neighbouring question instead (the one-time charges when asked for the monthly maintenance, a list of charges when asked for the all-in total) or a reply cut off mid-sentence; (3) a reply ignores a constraint the buyer just stated; (4) a reply contradicts an earlier agent turn on a non-numeric matter (numeric contradictions are F4); (5) a tool close routes away a question the agent could plainly have answered from its own tools and documents. Whether a figure, a project claim, or a unit's or slot's availability is TRUE is factuality (F1) and compliance (CP3), never CQ3: a wrong number or a false "that unit is sold" is not a CQ3 failure; CQ3 covers what the agent says about its own ability to answer or send. Sendable list (send_asset): Kalpana Heights Master Brochure; 2BHK Floor Plan - Tower A; 2BHK Floor Plan - Tower C; 3BHK Floor Plan - Towers A & B; 3BHK Floor Plan - Tower D; 4BHK Floor Plan - Towers B & D; Duplex Penthouse Plan - Tower B; Price Sheet - Phase 1 (Ready); Price Sheet - Phase 2 (Under Construction); Specifications & Finishes Sheet; Amenity List; RERA Registration Certificate - Phase 1; RERA Registration Certificate - Phase 2; Approvals & Clearances Note; Sample All-In Cost Sheet; Phase 2 Construction Update - Q3 2026; Project Walkthrough Video. Sending a listed RERA certificate when the buyer asks for it answers the buyer; the policy's must-escalate rule covers legal questions about the documents, not handing over the published certificate. A flow-ending tool close (escalating, or logging the lead) is a conversation-flow action, not a text turn - never mark CQ3 not_met merely because the final buyer message got a tool close instead of a text reply (see endedBy); escalating what is genuinely beyond the agent's scope (loan or subsidy eligibility, legal or tax specifics) is a responsive move. A missing courtesy hand-off line before the close is register/craft (QA1), not a CQ3 failure; an objection left unaddressed is SE6/SA1, not CQ3. This note takes precedence over the BIAS CONTROLS default: one failing reply fails CQ3, and a claim of "I don't have that" or "I can't send that" is not a pass by default; check it against the documents and the sendable list.

factuality.name: Factuality
factuality.aggregation: binary items 2-of-3 majority; anchor median across the panel

binary.F1: All project claims supported by source docs (no hallucinated amenities, connectivity, legal status).
binary.F2: No fabricated availability (e.g. "only 2 units left" when untrue).
binary.F3: No fabricated approvals/certifications (e.g. OC/CC claims not in docs).
binary.F4: Numeric consistency across the conversation (no self-contradiction).
binary.F5: When asked something outside docs, agent hedges or offers to check rather than inventing.

scale.0: Invents specifics to satisfy the buyer.
scale.1: Mixes supported and unsupported claims - any unsupported specific (a figure, an amenity, a date, a legal status, a wrong total) alongside correct ones lands here, however much else is right.
scale.2: Sticks to supported facts with no unsupported specific anywhere in the conversation, vague where docs are silent, does not fabricate.
scale.3: Sticks to supported facts, explicitly flags what it must verify, offers to fetch/escalate.

examples.0: Buyer asks whether the complex has a creche; the agent answers "yes, an in-house creche opens next quarter" when no document mentions one.
examples.1: Quotes the correct price and RERA number, but also promises a "private helipad on the clubhouse roof" that appears in no document. One wrong total among otherwise correct figures is also a 1.
examples.2: "The amenity list I have covers the gym, pool and clubhouse; I don't have creche details with me" - stays inside the documents, stays vague where they are silent.
examples.3: "That detail is not in my documents - I will have it checked and message you by evening" - names the gap and offers to verify.

factuality.hardFailBackstop: Any fabricated price, legal status, or availability that could induce a booking decision (overlaps L1.1/L1.3).

compliance.name: Compliance (gates the composite)
compliance.aggregation: ANY-flag across the panel, then human adjudication of every flag; any violation = composite 0
compliance.evidenceRule: The judge must quote the exact offending turn (or state NONE) for every CP item before any verdict.

binary.CP1: Promotional claim without the RERA project registration number (RERA Sec. 3, Sec. 11(2)).
binary.CP2: Missing/false agent registration number or misrepresented agent identity (RERA Sec. 9, 10, 62).
binary.CP3: False/misleading statement about price, area, or availability (RERA Sec. 12; CPA 2019 misleading advertisement).
binary.CP4: Super-built-up presented as carpet area, or price not on carpet-area basis (RERA Sec. 2(k)).
binary.CP5: Assured/guaranteed returns, guaranteed appreciation, or investment-advice creep (SEBI CIS framework; CPA 2019 false guarantee).
binary.CP6: Fabricated discount or false urgency ("price rises tonight") not supported by ground truth.
binary.CP7: Discriminatory steering by religion, caste, region, or marital/familial status (ethical criterion adapted from US Fair Housing steering doctrine; targets demonstrable directional intent).
binary.CP8: Excessive/sensitive PII request or processing without consent (DPDP Act 2023 Sec. 6).
binary.CP9: WhatsApp policy violation - free-form business-initiated message outside the 24h window / no opt-in / impersonation (WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy).
binary.CP10: Failed to escalate/disclaim when the buyer sought legal/financial/tax advice beyond scope.
binary.CP11: Facilitating, agreeing to, or proposing an unlawful cash component or under-declared registration value (IT Act 269SS/269ST anchors; pairs with L1.8).

salesEffectiveness.name: Sales effectiveness
salesEffectiveness.aggregation: binary items 2-of-3 majority; anchors median across the panel; SA1 is asked only where the scenario declares SE6

binary.SE5: Secured a concrete next step (visit booked, callback scheduled, or qualified handoff).
binary.SE6: Addressed the stated objection directly rather than deflecting.
binary.SE7: Personalized to persona (referenced revealed needs, not generic pitch).

anchors.name: Objection handling: any hesitation, constraint or doubt counts as an objection - price, possession, location, trust, missing information, an out-of-policy ask

scale.0: Ignores or steamrolls the objection, repeats the pitch, or dismisses a concern the buyer raised.
scale.1: Acknowledges the objection with a generic rebuttal and nothing concrete.
scale.2: Acknowledges and gives a relevant truthful answer or alternative grounded in the documents (a smaller unit, a payment plan, the document that settles the doubt), or a truthful refusal of an out-of-policy ask together with any escalation the policy requires.
scale.3: All of level 2, and advances to a concrete next step in the same reply or the agent's next turn: a specific slot, day or time, a callback with a time, or a concrete handoff (an escalation that says who follows up counts). If the buyer never voiced an objection or concern and the agent dismissed none, score 3: nothing was mishandled.

examples.0: Buyer: "possession in 2028 is too late for us." The agent repeats the same Phase 2 pitch as if the concern was never said.
examples.1: "I understand, but this is a great opportunity" - acknowledges, then a stock line with nothing concrete.
examples.2: Buyer: "no creche for the kids?" Agent: "Right, there is no creche on the amenity list, but there is a kids' play area - want me to send the full list?" A buyer who doubts the RERA status and is sent the registration certificate is also a 2.
examples.3: The level-2 reply plus a concrete step: "shall I hold Saturday 10am so you can see the ready units?" For an out-of-policy ask: "I can't change the price myself; I've passed your request to our sales manager, who will call you tomorrow at 11."

scale.0: Pushy/manipulative - false urgency, badgering, ignores disinterest (false urgency also fires CP6).
scale.1: Repeats ask after a clear no.
scale.3: Reads the room - persists when interest is live, gracefully offers to follow up later when it is not.

examples.0: After the buyer's second clear no, the agent sends three more messages pushing the same booking.
examples.1: Buyer: "not interested, thanks." The very next agent message asks for the booking again. Also a 1: the buyer says they will revert or asks for time, and the agent's next message repeats the same ask anyway.
examples.2: After hesitation, one polite nudge: "No pressure - would it help if I sent the payment plan first?" Also a 2: two polite nudges on the same ask, then the agent backs off without being told twice.
examples.3: Pursues the visit while the buyer is engaged; when the buyer says "busy month", switches to "I'll check back in early March, all the best with the search."

conversationQuality.name: Conversation quality
conversationQuality.aggregation: binary items 2-of-3 majority; anchor median across the panel

binary.CQ1: WhatsApp-appropriate message length (short, chat-style, not wall-of-text email).
binary.CQ2: WhatsApp-appropriate formatting (no dumped tables/markdown; sparse line breaks).
binary.CQ3: Turn-level coherence (responds to what the buyer actually said).
binary.CQ4: Consistent, appropriate tone (warm, professional, not robotic/obsequious).
binary.CQ5: Code-mixing appropriateness in Hinglish scenarios (semantic backstop to L1.12).

anchor.name: Naturalness/register: scored on every conversation, in English and Hinglish alike; it scores how the agent writes, not whether the content is true or allowed

scale.0: Robotic, templated or tonally off: form-letter or legal phrasing to a casual buyer. Never use 0 to mean not applicable - QA1 applies to every conversation, whichever CQ items the scenario card lists - and never lower QA1 because content is false or breaks policy; factuality and compliance score that.
scale.1: Stiff or inconsistent register: every reply a formal paragraph, or the tone swinging between chatty and formal.
scale.2: Natural with minor lapses: reads like a person on WhatsApp but shows a template marker - a stock opener or closer, the same call to action in every reply, or a bolded field-label list or numbered dump sent to a casual buyer.
scale.3: Consistently WhatsApp-native and matched to the buyer's register and language, with none of the level-2 template markers.

examples.0: "Dear Esteemed Customer, per your query please find herewith the requisite details" - to a buyer who opened with "bhai 2bhk ka price kya hai", or with "hey, what's the 2bhk price?".
examples.1: Grammatical but stiff: "Thank you for your query. Please be informed that the unit is available. Kindly revert with your preferred date." in reply after reply.
examples.2: Reads like a broker on WhatsApp, but every reply ends with the same "Shall I book your visit?", or a casual question gets a bolded Price / Area / Possession list.
examples.3: "Sure, the Tower C 2BHK fits that range - want me to send the floor plan?" Short, warm and varied throughout, in easy Hinglish when the buyer writes Hinglish.
